column1: # Fixed request set for results-API conformance checks (design W11, step 3).
# Lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored.
# Chosen to cover each distinct code path in api/app/server rather than to be
# exhaustive: the two-bucket read fallback, the badge redirect, input rejection,
# and the CORS headers the project website depends on. Add cases here rather
# than passing ad-hoc URLs, so that a comparison run is reproducible and so the
# same set is used before and after a cutover.
# Deliberately NOT included: the POST publish path. It has side effects
# (verification against live Sigstore, a write to the results bucket, a CDN
# purge) and cannot be exercised safely against production. Confirming it is a
# separate cutover step -- watch a real Scorecard Action upload land.
# A repository certain to have published results.
# A high-traffic repository, likely served from the Action-published bucket
# rather than the weekly cron bucket -- the two-bucket fallback in
# get_results.go means these can resolve differently.
# A repository scanned by the weekly cron but unlikely to publish via the
# GitLab-hosted, to confirm platform routing is not GitHub-specific.
# Path traversal, which sanitizeInputs is meant to reject.
# --- Badge: a redirect, one case per documented style --------------------
# --- CORS: the project website is a browser client of this API -----------
# The viewer at scorecard.dev fetches results cross-origin, so the response
# headers matter as much as the body.
